page.title: Variation Board
page.purpose: Let an operator compare a candidate set on evidence and converge it to one committed output, without the interface nudging the choice toward the most familiar option.

priorities.statement: What is actually different between these candidates
Which candidates are ineligible, and for exactly which named reason
How varied this set is overall, and on what basis that number is computed
What has already been pinned or rejected, and therefore what a reroll will change

elements.name: Candidate
elements.description: One candidate. Text first and generously sized; measurements as a chip row beneath. Never a headline score.

elements.name: Measurements
elements.description: Reading grade, burstiness sparkline, lexicon flags, axis cell. Each carries text, never colour alone.

elements.name: Ineligibility reason
elements.description: The named constraint a candidate failed. Present on the card; the candidate is retained in the set, never hidden.

elements.name: Set diversity
elements.description: One number for the whole set with its basis named inline. Never a bare figure.

elements.name: Pin
elements.description: Protects a candidate from the next reroll. Keyboard reachable without a pointer.

elements.name: Reject
elements.description: Records a rejection that becomes negative conditioning on reroll.

elements.name: None of these
elements.description: First-class action. Rerolls the whole set conditioned against everything rejected so far.

elements.name: Commit
elements.description: Commits one candidate. States its reason inline whenever unavailable.

elements.name: Sort
elements.description: Explicit operator-chosen ordering. Defaults to generation order or axis cell, never to a quality proxy.

states.description: A returned candidate set at rest.
A round is in flight; prior candidates stay visible and comparable.
Some candidates failed a hard constraint and are shown with their named reason rather than removed.
Every candidate failed. The set is retained, commit is unavailable, and the blocking constraint is named.
No round has been run yet for this session.
The per-session budget ceiling refused further generation, naming the ceiling.
Inference is unreachable. Existing candidates remain readable and comparable; generation is refused by name.
Data for this surface is in flight; skeleton structure is shown rather than a blank frame.
Some data resolved and some did not; what resolved stays usable and what failed is named rather than silently omitted.
Displayed data is known to be out of date relative to its source; the surface says so rather than presenting it as current.
The request failed; the specific cause is stated inline and the surface offers the action that retries it.

claims.statement: No candidate card presents a single aggregate quality score anywhere in the set view.
claims.rationale: The scenario's central design rule. A single number invites ranking, and ranking by taste re-imposes the typicality bias the whole scenario exists to counteract. A feature vector invites reading instead. (Tier: aspirational until the UI exists and accessibility captures can join these bindings; promote to machine at that point — the binding testids above are the contract the UI must satisfy.)

claims.statement: The set carries no default ordering by any quality proxy; ordering is generation order or axis cell until the operator explicitly re-sorts.
claims.rationale: Ordering is a nudge. Ordering by the model's own uncalibrated ordering signal would be a nudge derived from a number already declared meaningless. (Tier: aspirational until the UI exists and accessibility captures can join these bindings; promote to machine at that point — the binding testids above are the contract the UI must satisfy.)

claims.statement: An ineligible candidate is perceivably distinct from an eligible one and states its named failing constraint, rather than being absent from the set.
claims.rationale: Dropping ineligible candidates would hide the shape of the distribution and make a constraint look like a generation failure. (Tier: aspirational until the UI exists and accessibility captures can join these bindings; promote to machine at that point — the binding testids above are the contract the UI must satisfy.)

claims.statement: Set diversity is always shown with the metric basis that produced it.
claims.rationale: A bare diversity number is not interpretable and invites comparison across sets that are not comparable. (Tier: aspirational until the UI exists and accessibility captures can join these bindings; promote to machine at that point — the binding testids above are the contract the UI must satisfy.)

claims.statement: Whenever commit is unavailable its specific cause is stated inline.
claims.rationale: A dead control with no explanation is the failure this surface exists to prevent. (Tier: aspirational until the UI exists and accessibility captures can join these bindings; promote to machine at that point — the binding testids above are the contract the UI must satisfy.)

claims.statement: Every sparkline carries a text alternative stating its underlying numbers.
claims.rationale: Measurement is the product. A screen-reader user must compare candidates on the same evidence a sighted user sees. (Tier: aspirational until the UI exists and accessibility captures can join these bindings; promote to machine at that point — the binding testids above are the contract the UI must satisfy.)

claims.statement: Pin, reject, and commit are reachable and operable by keyboard alone across the whole set.
claims.rationale: Converging a set is the primary task; it must not require a pointer. (Tier: aspirational until the UI exists and accessibility captures can join these bindings; promote to machine at that point — the binding testids above are the contract the UI must satisfy.)

claims.statement: On mobile the set becomes a stepwise panel sequence preserving comparison context rather than a shrunken grid.
claims.rationale: Comparing two long passages in a narrow column is the one degradation this surface must not accept.
